hints: Look at what all four bullet points have in common. Are any of them about making gametes or a new organism by sexual reproduction?
Remember the key rule: mitosis for growth, replacement, repair and asexual reproduction always makes genetically identical daughter cells, while only meiosis makes genetically different cells.
walkthrough:
**Recall what genetically identical means**

Think of it simply. Genetically identical cells are made by copying the parent cell exactly, with no mixing of genes.

That process is mitosis:
$$mitosis \rightarrow 2 \text{ genetically identical daughter cells}$$

**Test each process in the list**

Growth of plant roots is cell division by mitosis in the meristem to make more identical root cells.

Replacement of dead human skin cells is mitosis to make identical skin cells. Repair of damaged muscle tissue is mitosis to make identical muscle cells. Asexual reproduction of coral involves only one parent and mitosis, so no variation.

**Count them up**

All four processes use mitosis and no meiosis or fertilisation is involved.

So all 4 produce genetically identical cells, which matches option D.

options.A: Not correct. Far more than 1 process uses mitosis to make identical cells, so 1 is too low.
options.B: Not correct. Growth, replacement, repair and asexual reproduction all give identical cells, not just 2 of them.
options.C: Not correct. It is tempting to exclude asexual reproduction, but it also uses mitosis so all 4 count, not just 3.
options.D: Correct and well done. All 4 processes involve mitosis only, so all 4 produce genetically identical cells.
